target_audience: High school or introductory college statistics students

sections.title: The Foundation: Bernoulli Trials
lecture_lines: Bernoulli trials are the building blocks of binomial distributions.
Meet Finn. Every fly catch is a single trial.
Success means he catches the fly.
Failure means the fly escapes.
Finn's success rate stays constant at seventy percent.
animations: [self.wait(2.0)] Fade in title 'Bernoulli Trial: Success or Failure' in #FFFFFF.
[self.wait(1.5)] Create Frog object Finn (#00FF00) and Fly object.
[self.wait(1.5)] Fly moves to Finn; Finn catches it. Success: #FFD700.
[self.wait(1.5)] Fly escapes Finn's tongue. Failure: #A9A9A9.
[self.wait(2.0)] Highlight 'p = 0.70' in #FFD700 using SurroundingRectangle.

sections.title: The BINS Criteria
lecture_lines: We use 'BINS' to check if a scenario fits.
First, trials must have only two Binary outcomes.
Second, every trial must be Independent of others.
Third, there must be a fixed Number of trials.
Finally, the probability 'p' must be the Same.
animations: [self.wait(2.0)] Fade in 'BINS Criteria' header in #FFFFFF.
[self.wait(1.5)] Display 'Binary' with a checkmark in #00FF00.
[self.wait(1.5)] Display 'Independent' with a checkmark in #00FF00.
[self.wait(1.5)] Display 'Number (n=10)' with a checkmark in #00FF00.
[self.wait(1.5)] Display 'Same p' with a checkmark in #00FF00.

sections.title: The Mathematical Recipe (The Formula)
lecture_lines: The formula calculates the probability of exactly k successes.
'n choose k' counts the different ways to succeed.
'p' to the 'k' represents the successes' probability.
'1 minus p' to the 'n-k' represents failures.
Combine these parts to find the total probability.
animations: [self.wait(2.0)] Fade in formula: P(X=k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k).
[self.wait(1.5)] Color 'nCk' Magenta (#FF00FF) and label it 'Combinations'.
[self.wait(1.5)] Color 'p^k' Cyan (#00FFFF) and label 'Success Prob'.
[self.wait(1.5)] Color '(1-p)^(n-k)' Yellow (#FFFF00) and label 'Failure Prob'.
[self.wait(2.0)] Morph variables into values: 10C7 * 0.7^7 * 0.3^3.

sections.title: Visualizing the Distribution
lecture_lines: A histogram shows probabilities for all possible outcomes.
Changing 'p' shifts the distribution's shape and peak.
The tallest bar shows the most likely outcome.
animations: [self.wait(2.0)] Create BarChart for n=10, p=0.5 in Blue (#ADD8E6).
[self.wait(2.0)] Smoothly morph BarChart to n=10, p=0.7 in Green (#90EE90).
[self.wait(1.5)] Highlight bar at k=7 with Flash and color #FF4500.

sections.title: Application and Summary
lecture_lines: Binomial distributions help us predict real-world outcomes.
Quality control uses this to find defect probabilities.
It's a powerful tool for repeated, independent trials.
animations: [self.wait(2.0)] Fade in Robot icon (#C0C0C0) and 100 circuit boards.
[self.wait(1.5)] Highlight defective circuit boards in Red (#FF0000).
[self.wait(2.0)] Fade out icons; show summary text in #FFFFFF.
